history2.fixtures.table_summary: The 'history2.fixtures' table stores detailed information about cricket match fixtures, including match details, participating teams, venue information, and match outcomes. It serves as a historical record for cricket matches, allowing for analysis of match results, team performances, and player statistics within various leagues and seasons.

id.description: Primary key (bigint) uniquely identifying each fixture.

league_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the league in which the match is played.

season_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the season of the match.

stage_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) indicating the stage of the league (e.g., group, knockout).

round.description: Stores the round of the match (varchar), indicating its sequence in the league.

localteam_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the local team playing in the match.

visitorteam_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the visiting team playing in the match.

starting_at.description: Stores the date and time (datetime) when the match is scheduled to start.

type.description: Stores the type of match (varchar), such as T20I, ODI, etc.

live.description: Indicates if the match is currently live (bit).

status.description: Stores the current status of the match (varchar), such as Finished, Abandoned, etc.

note.description: Stores additional notes about the match outcome (varchar).

toss_won_team_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the team that won the toss.

first_umpire_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the first umpire officiating the match.

second_umpire_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the second umpire officiating the match.

tv_umpire_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the TV umpire, if applicable.

referee_id.description: Foreign key (bigint) referencing the match referee.

elected.description: Stores the decision made by the toss-winning team (varchar), such as batting or bowling.

history2.fixtures__balls.table_summary: The fixtures__balls table stores detailed information about each ball bowled in a cricket match, including the players involved (batsman and bowler), the score resulting from each ball, and the context of the match (fixture and teams). This allows for comprehensive ball-by-ball analysis of cricket matches.

id.description: A unique identifier for each ball entry, stored as a bigint. This serves as the primary key for the table.

fixture_id.description: References the match fixture, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the fixtures table, indicating which match this ball belongs to.

team_id.description: Identifies the team that bowled the ball, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the teams table.

ball.description: Represents the specific ball in decimal format (e.g., 6.5 for the 6th over, 5th ball), stored as a real. It is crucial for understanding the sequence of play.

scoreboard.description: Indicates the scoreboard designation (S1 for bowling team, S2 for batting team), stored as a varchar. This helps in identifying which team is currently batting or bowling.

batsman_id.description: References the batsman who faced the ball, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the players table.

bowler_id.description: References the bowler who delivered the ball, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the players table.

score_id.description: References the score entry for the ball, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the scores table, which details the outcome of the ball.

batsman__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the batsman, stored as a varchar. It indicates that the batsman is a player.

batsman__id.description: Unique identifier for the batsman, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the players table.

batsman__country_id.description: References the country of the batsman, stored as a bigint. This links to a countries table, if available.

batsman__firstname.description: The first name of the batsman, stored as a varchar.

batsman__lastname.description: The last name of the batsman, stored as a varchar.

batsman__fullname.description: The full name of the batsman, stored as a varchar. This may not be present in all tables.

batsman__image_path.description: URL to the batsman's image, stored as a varchar.

batsman__dateofbirth.description: The birth date of the batsman, stored as a varchar. Ensure proper date formatting.

batsman__gender.description: The gender of the batsman, stored as a varchar.

batsman__battingstyle.description: The batting style of the batsman, stored as a varchar.

batsman__bowlingstyle.description: The bowling style of the batsman, stored as a varchar.

batsman__position__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the batsman's position, stored as a varchar.

batsman__position__id.description: Identifier for the batsman's position, stored as a bigint.

batsman__position__name.description: The name of the batsman's position, stored as a varchar.

batsman__updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update of batsman information, stored as a datetime.

bowler__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__id.description: Unique identifier for the bowler, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the players table.

bowler__country_id.description: References the country of the bowler, stored as a bigint. This links to a countries table, if available.

bowler__firstname.description: The first name of the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__lastname.description: The last name of the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__fullname.description: The full name of the bowler, stored as a varchar. This may not be present in all tables.

bowler__image_path.description: URL to the bowler's image, stored as a varchar.

bowler__dateofbirth.description: The birth date of the bowler, stored as a varchar. Ensure proper date formatting.

bowler__gender.description: The gender of the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__battingstyle.description: The batting style of the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__bowlingstyle.description: The bowling style of the bowler, stored as a varchar.

bowler__position__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the bowler's position, stored as a varchar.

bowler__position__id.description: Identifier for the bowler's position, stored as a bigint.

bowler__position__name.description: The name of the bowler's position, stored as a varchar.

bowler__updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update of bowler information, stored as a datetime.

score__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the score, stored as a varchar.

score__id.description: Unique identifier for the score entry, stored as a bigint. This is a primary key in the scores table.

score__name.description: Describes the score outcome (e.g., 'No Run', '1 Run'), stored as a varchar.

score__runs.description: The number of runs scored from the ball, stored as a bigint. This is critical for calculating match statistics.

score__four.description: Indicates if a four was scored, stored as a bit.

score__six.description: Indicates if a six was scored, stored as a bit.

score__bye.description: The number of byes scored, stored as a bigint.

score__leg_bye.description: The number of leg byes scored, stored as a bigint.

score__noball.description: The number of no balls, stored as a bigint.

score__noball_runs.description: The runs scored from no balls, stored as a bigint.

score__is_wicket.description: Indicates if a wicket fell on this ball, stored as a bit.

score__ball.description: Indicates if this entry represents a ball bowled, stored as a bit.

score__out.description: Indicates if the batsman is out, stored as a bit.

team__resource.description: Stores the resource type for the team, stored as a varchar.

team__id.description: Unique identifier for the team, stored as a bigint. This is a foreign key linking to the teams table.

team__name.description: The name of the team, stored as a varchar.

team__code.description: The code of the team, stored as a varchar.

team__image_path.description: URL to the team's image, stored as a varchar.

team__country_id.description: References the country of the team, stored as a bigint. This links to a countries table, if available.

team__national_team.description: Indicates if the team is a national team, stored as a bit.

team__updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update of team information, stored as a datetime.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update of the ball entry, stored as a datetime.

catchstump_id.description: References any catch or stump event, stored as a bigint. This may link to a separate events table.

batsmanout_id.description: References the batsman who is out, stored as a bigint. This may link to a separate players table.

batsman_one_on_creeze_id.description: References the first batsman on the crease, stored as a bigint. This may link to a separate players table.

batsman_two_on_creeze_id.description: References the second batsman on the crease, stored as a bigint. This may link to a separate players table.

history2.fixtures__batting.table_summary: The fixtures__batting table stores detailed statistics for each batting performance in cricket matches, capturing data on individual players' contributions, including runs scored, boundaries hit, and the context of their dismissals within specific fixtures.

id.description: A unique identifier for each batting record. Data type: bigint. This serves as the primary key for the table.

fixture_id.description: Links to the specific match fixture in which the batting occurred. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the fixtures table.

team_id.description: Identifies the team for which the player batted. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the teams table.

scoreboard.description: Denotes the scoreboard designation (S1 for bowling team, S2 for batting team). Data type: varchar. Important for understanding the context of the batting performance.

player_id.description: Identifies the player who batted. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the players table.

wicket_id.description: Links to the specific wicket associated with the player's dismissal. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the wickets table.

ball.description: Represents the specific ball number within the over when the batting action occurred. Data type: bigint. Should be interpreted in the context of overs (e.g., 5.3 for the 5th over, 3rd ball).

score_id.description: Links to a unique score entry for the batting action. Data type: bigint. This may relate to other score-related tables.

score.description: Records the runs scored on that specific ball. Data type: bigint. Important to differentiate from total innings score.

four_x.description: Counts the number of fours hit on that ball. Data type: bigint. Useful for boundary statistics.

six_x.description: Counts the number of sixes hit on that ball. Data type: bigint. Useful for boundary statistics.

bowling_player_id.description: Identifies the bowler who delivered the ball. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the players table.

fow_score.description: Records the score at the time of the wicket falling. Data type: bigint. Important for understanding the match context.

fow_balls.description: Indicates the number of balls faced before the wicket fell. Data type: real. Useful for analyzing batting partnerships.

rate.description: Represents the scoring rate at which the player was batting at that moment. Data type: real. Important for performance analysis.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to the record. Data type: datetime. Useful for tracking data changes.

catch_stump_player_id.description: Identifies the player involved in the dismissal (if applicable). Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key referencing the players table.

columns.\u274c NO 'batsman__fullname': Join to fixtures__balls for batsman names

history2.fixtures__bowling.table_summary: The fixtures__bowling table stores detailed statistics for bowlers in cricket matches, capturing performance metrics such as overs bowled, runs conceded, wickets taken, and other relevant bowling data for each fixture. This data is crucial for analyzing individual bowler performance within specific matches.

id.description: A unique identifier for each bowling record (bigint). This serves as the primary key for the table.

fixture_id.description: Links to the specific match or fixture (bigint). This is a foreign key that connects to the fixtures table, allowing for the association of bowling data with the corresponding match.

team_id.description: Identifies the team for which the bowler is playing (bigint). This is a foreign key that relates to the teams table, linking bowlers to their respective teams.

scoreboard.description: Represents the scoreboard identifier (varchar). 'S1' indicates the bowling team, while 'S2' indicates the batting team. Misuse may occur if the context of the scoreboard is not understood.

player_id.description: Identifies the bowler (bigint). This is a foreign key that connects to the players table, allowing for the retrieval of bowler-specific information such as names.

overs.description: Records the number of overs bowled in decimal format (real). It is crucial for understanding the bowler's contribution but should be interpreted correctly as it represents overs and balls.

medians.description: Stores the number of median deliveries (bigint). This metric is less commonly used and may require additional context for interpretation.

runs.description: Captures the total runs conceded by the bowler (bigint). This is a key performance metric and should be used in conjunction with overs and wickets for analysis.

wickets.description: Records the number of wickets taken by the bowler (bigint). It is essential for evaluating bowler effectiveness but should be noted that it refers to wickets taken, not remaining.

wide.description: Counts the number of wide deliveries bowled (bigint). This metric is important for understanding the bowler's accuracy.

noball.description: Counts the number of no-balls bowled (bigint). Similar to wides, this metric reflects the bowler's discipline and should be monitored.

rate.description: Calculates the bowling economy rate (real). This is a critical metric for assessing a bowler's efficiency in conceding runs.

updated_at.description: Records the timestamp of the last update to the bowling record (datetime). Useful for tracking data changes but not for analysis.

columns.\u274c NO 'score': Use 'runs' for runs conceded in fixtures__bowling
columns.\u274c NO 'batsman__fullname': Join to fixtures__balls for batsman names
columns.\u274c NO 'bowler__fullname': CRITICAL: Join to fixtures__balls for bowler names!
columns.\u274c NO 'batsman_id': Join to fixtures__balls for batsman information

history2.fixtures__lineup.table_summary: This table stores information about the player lineups for cricket matches, including details about each player's identity, role, and attributes within a specific match lineup. It is crucial for analyzing team compositions and player statistics in the context of cricket matches.

id.description: Stores the unique identifier for each player. Data type: bigint. This serves as a primary key for player records.

country_id.description: Stores the identifier for the country the player represents. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key that links to a countries table, allowing for country-specific queries.

firstname.description: Stores the player's first name. Data type: varchar. This is part of the player's identity.

lastname.description: Stores the player's last name. Data type: varchar. This is part of the player's identity.

fullname.description: Stores the full name of the player. Data type: varchar. This is used for display purposes and may be referenced in other tables.

image_path.description: Stores the URL to the player's image. Data type: varchar. This is used for visual representation in applications.

dateofbirth.description: Stores the player's date of birth. Data type: varchar. This is important for age-related statistics but should be validated for date format.

gender.description: Stores the gender of the player. Data type: varchar. This is relevant for demographic analysis.

battingstyle.description: Stores the batting style of the player (e.g., left-hand-bat). Data type: varchar. This is important for understanding player capabilities.

position__resource.description: Stores the type of position resource, typically 'positions'. Data type: varchar. This helps identify the nature of the position record.

position__id.description: Stores the unique identifier for the player's position. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key linking to a positions table.

position__name.description: Stores the name of the player's position (e.g., Batsman, Allrounder). Data type: varchar. This is used for categorization within the lineup.

updated_at.description: Stores the timestamp of the last update to the record. Data type: datetime. This is useful for tracking changes over time.

lineup__team_id.description: Stores the identifier for the team in which the player is lined up. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key linking to a teams table.

lineup__captain.description: Indicates whether the player is the captain of the team. Data type: bit. This is a boolean value that should be used correctly to avoid misinterpretation.

lineup__wicketkeeper.description: Indicates whether the player is the wicketkeeper. Data type: bit. This is a boolean value that should be used correctly to avoid misinterpretation.

lineup__substitution.description: Indicates whether the player is a substitute. Data type: bit. This is a boolean value that should be used correctly to avoid misinterpretation.

bowlingstyle.description: Stores the bowling style of the player (e.g., right-arm-fast-medium). Data type: varchar. This is important for understanding player capabilities.

history2.fixtures__runs.table_summary: The fixtures__runs table stores detailed information about the runs scored by each team in a cricket match, organized by innings. It captures metrics such as score, wickets lost, overs bowled, and powerplay details, allowing for analysis of team performance in specific fixtures.

id.description: A bigint that serves as a unique identifier for each run entry. It is not a primary key but is essential for distinguishing between different run records.

fixture_id.description: A bigint that acts as a foreign key linking to the specific match fixture in another table. It is crucial for associating runs with the correct match context.

team_id.description: A bigint that serves as a foreign key referencing the team involved in the innings. It is important for identifying which team the runs belong to.

inning.description: A bigint indicating the inning number (1 or 2) for the runs scored. It is important for distinguishing between the first and second innings of a match.

updated_at.description: A datetime that records the last update time for the run entry. It is useful for tracking changes but does not play a role in the primary data analysis.

score.description: A bigint representing the total runs scored by the team in that inning at the time of the entry. It is important to note that 'score' can have different meanings in different contexts, so it should be used carefully.

wickets.description: A bigint indicating the number of wickets lost by the batting team in that inning. It is crucial for understanding team performance and should not be confused with wickets in hand.

overs.description: A real number representing the overs bowled at the time of the entry, in decimal format (e.g., 10.0 for 10 overs). It is essential for analyzing the progression of the innings.

pp1.description: A varchar that indicates the runs scored during the first powerplay. It is important for understanding scoring patterns but may not always be populated.

pp2.description: A varchar that indicates the runs scored during the second powerplay. Similar to pp1, it may not always be populated and should be interpreted with caution.

pp3.description: A varchar that indicates the runs scored during the third powerplay. It may not always be populated and should be used carefully in analysis.

columns.\u274c NO 'batsman__fullname': Join to fixtures__balls for player names
columns.\u274c NO 'bowler__fullname': Join to fixtures__balls for player names

history2.fixtures__scoreboards.table_summary: The fixtures__scoreboards table stores detailed statistics for cricket matches, specifically tracking the scoreboards for each team during a fixture. It includes metrics related to runs scored, extras, overs bowled, and wickets lost, allowing for comprehensive analysis of match progress and performance.

id.description: A unique identifier for each scoreboard entry, stored as a bigint. This serves as a primary key for the table.

fixture_id.description: A bigint that links to the specific match fixture, acting as a foreign key to relate this table to the fixtures table.

team_id.description: A bigint that identifies the team associated with the scoreboard entry, serving as a foreign key to the teams table.

type.description: A varchar indicating the type of scoreboard entry (e.g., total or extra). This helps differentiate between overall scores and additional runs.

scoreboard.description: A varchar representing the scoreboard identifier (e.g., S1 for the bowling team, S2 for the batting team). It is crucial for distinguishing between teams in the context of a match.

wide.description: A bigint representing the number of wide balls bowled, contributing to the extras in the total score.

noball_runs.description: A bigint indicating the runs scored from no balls, which are counted as extras.

noball_balls.description: A bigint that counts the number of no balls bowled, relevant for understanding the impact of no balls on the game.

bye.description: A bigint representing runs scored from byes, which are also counted as extras.

leg_bye.description: A bigint indicating runs scored from leg byes, contributing to the extras.

penalty.description: A bigint that records any penalty runs awarded, which are rare but can affect the total score.

total.description: A bigint representing the total runs scored by the team at that point in the match. It is important to note that this may represent different contexts (per-ball vs innings total) depending on the table.

overs.description: A real number indicating the overs bowled in decimal format (e.g., 10.0 for 10 overs). This is crucial for understanding the match's progress.

wickets.description: A bigint representing the number of wickets lost by the team, which is critical for assessing the team's performance.

updated_at.description: A datetime indicating when the scoreboard entry was last updated, useful for tracking changes over time.

history2.leagues.table_summary: The 'history2.leagues' table stores information about various cricket leagues and tournaments, including details such as their names, codes, and associated seasons and countries. This table is essential for categorizing and referencing different cricket competitions within the broader statistics database.

id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each league. Data type: bigint. This is a primary key that uniquely identifies each record in the table.

season_id.description: Stores the identifier for the season associated with the league. Data type: bigint. This is a foreign key that links to a seasons table, providing context for when the league occurs.

lastname.description: Stores the last name of the official. Data type: varchar. This is used for display purposes and should be combined with firstname for full names.

history2.players.table_summary: The history2.players table stores detailed information about cricket players, including their personal details, playing styles, and positions. id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each player. Data type: bigint. Role: Primary key. This ID is crucial for linking to player-specific statistics in other tables.

country_id.description: Stores the identifier for the country the player represents. Data type: bigint. Role: Foreign key. This links to a countries table, allowing for country-based queries.

firstname.description: Stores the player's first name. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Useful for displaying player names.

lastname.description: Stores the player's last name. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Useful for displaying player names.

fullname.description: Stores the full name of the player, combining firstname and lastname. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Important for clarity in reports and statistics.

image_path.description: Stores the URL to the player's image. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Useful for displaying player profiles in applications.

dateofbirth.description: Stores the player's date of birth. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Important for age-related statistics but should be validated for date format.

gender.description: Stores the player's gender. Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Important for demographic analysis.

battingstyle.description: Stores the player's batting style (e.g., right-hand-bat). Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Useful for understanding player capabilities.

bowlingstyle.description: Stores the player's bowling style (e.g., right-arm-fast-medium). Data type: varchar. Role: Descriptive attribute. Useful for understanding player capabilities.

position__resource.description: Stores the type of position resource, specifically 'positions'. Data type: varchar. Role: Identifier for the position type.

history2.positions.table_summary: The history2.positions table stores the various player positions in cricket, such as Batsman and Bowler. This information is essential for categorizing player roles within match statistics and for linking player performance data to their respective positions.

id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each position, data type is bigint. This column serves as a unique identifier for the position and can be used as a foreign key in other tables to link player statistics to their respective roles.

name.description: Stores the name of the position (e.g., Batsman, Bowler), data type is varchar. This column provides a human-readable description of the position and is essential for understanding player roles in match data.

history2.scores.table_summary: The history2.scores table stores detailed statistics for each ball bowled in a cricket match, including runs scored, extras, and wicket information. It is used to analyze individual ball outcomes and contribute to overall match statistics.

id.description: A bigint that serves as a unique identifier for each score entry. It is not a primary key but should be unique within this table.

name.description: A varchar that describes the type of score event (e.g., '1 Bye'). This column provides context for the score but does not serve as a key.

runs.description: A bigint representing the number of runs scored on that particular ball. This metric is crucial for calculating individual and team scores.

four.description: A bit indicating whether the score includes a boundary (four runs). It is a boolean value and should be used to analyze scoring patterns.

six.description: A bit indicating whether the score includes a six (six runs). Similar to 'four', it is a boolean value for scoring analysis.

bye.description: A bigint representing the number of byes scored on that ball. This is an important metric for understanding extras in the game.

leg_bye.description: A bigint representing the number of leg byes scored. It is also an extra and should be considered in total extras calculations.

noball.description: A bigint indicating the number of no-balls bowled. This metric is important for understanding the impact of bowling infractions.

noball_runs.description: A bigint representing the runs awarded due to no-balls. This is crucial for calculating total runs in the match.

is_wicket.description: A bit indicating whether the ball resulted in a wicket. This boolean value is critical for analyzing bowling performance.

ball.description: A bit indicating whether this entry corresponds to a valid ball bowled. It should be used to filter valid scoring events.

out.description: A bit indicating whether the batsman is out on this ball. This is important for understanding the outcome of the delivery.

history2.seasons.table_summary: The 'history2.seasons' table stores information about different cricket seasons, including their unique identifiers, associated leagues, and relevant metadata. This table is essential for linking match data to specific seasons, allowing for historical analysis and season-based statistics.

id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each season, which is a big integer (bigint). This serves as the primary key for the table, uniquely identifying each record. It should not be confused with other identifiers in different tables.

league_id.description: Stores the identifier for the league associated with the season, which is a big integer (bigint). This acts as a foreign key linking to a leagues table, allowing for the association of seasons with specific leagues. Care should be taken to ensure that the league_id corresponds to valid entries in the leagues table.

name.description: Stores the name of the season, which is a string (varchar). This typically represents the year of the season (e.g., '2019'). It is not a primary key but is useful for human-readable references.

code.description: Stores a code for the season, which is a string (varchar). This is often the same as the name and serves as a shorthand reference. It is not a primary key but should be unique within the context of the table.

updated_at.description: Stores the timestamp of the last update to the record, which is a datetime. This column is useful for tracking changes and ensuring data integrity over time.

history2.stages.table_summary: The 'history2.stages' table stores information about different stages or groups within a cricket league for a specific season. Each entry represents a distinct stage, such as a group or knockout round, and includes metadata about the league and season it belongs to. This is crucial for organizing matches and standings within the league structure.

id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each stage, which is a bigint. This serves as the primary key for the table. It should not be confused with foreign keys from other tables.

league_id.description: Stores the identifier for the league to which the stage belongs, which is a bigint. This acts as a foreign key linking to a leagues table, ensuring that stages are correctly associated with their respective leagues.

season_id.description: Stores the identifier for the season in which the stage occurs, which is a bigint. This is a foreign key that connects to a seasons table, allowing for the organization of stages by season.

name.description: Stores the name of the stage, which is a varchar. This provides a human-readable identifier for the stage, such as 'Group A' or 'Group B'. It should not be used as a unique identifier.

code.description: Stores a short code for the stage, which is a varchar. This is often used for quick references and should be unique within the context of the league.

type.description: Stores the type of stage, which is a varchar. It indicates whether the stage is a league, knockout, etc. Misuse could occur if the type is assumed to be the same across different leagues.

standings.description: Stores a bit indicating whether standings are available for the stage. This is crucial for determining if performance metrics can be derived from this stage. Misinterpretation could arise if it is assumed that standings are always present.

updated_at.description: Stores the timestamp of the last update to the stage record, which is a datetime. This is important for tracking changes and should not be confused with creation timestamps.

history2.teams.table_summary: The history2.teams table stores information about cricket teams, including both national teams and franchise teams. It is used to identify teams in various cricket matches and tournaments, linking them to their respective countries and providing metadata such as team codes and images.

id.description: Stores the unique identifier for each team, which is a big integer (bigint). This serves as the primary key for the table, ensuring each team can be uniquely identified.

name.description: Stores the full name of the team, which is a string (varchar). This column is used for display purposes and is not a primary key. It should be unique for national teams but may not be for franchise teams.

code.description: Stores the abbreviated code for the team, which is a string (varchar). This is often used in match statistics and should be unique for each team.

image_path.description: Stores the URL of the team's logo or image, which is a string (varchar). This is used for visual representation in applications and does not serve as a key.

country_id.description: Stores the identifier for the country associated with the team, which is a big integer (bigint). This can be a foreign key linking to a countries table, providing context about the team's national affiliation.

national_team.description: Stores a boolean value (bit) indicating whether the team is a national team (True) or a franchise team (False). This is important for filtering queries based on team types.

updated_at.description: Stores the timestamp of the last update to the team's information, which is a datetime. This is useful for tracking changes and should be used with caution to avoid confusion with creation timestamps.

history2.venues.table_summary: The history2.venues table stores information about cricket venues, including their names, locations, capacities, and facilities. This is essential for linking match data to specific locations where cricket events take place.

id.description: Stores a unique identifier for each venue, which is a bigint. This serves as the primary key for the table and should be used to reference venues in other tables.

country_id.description: Stores the identifier for the country where the venue is located, which is a bigint. This acts as a foreign key linking to a countries table, allowing for country-specific queries. Ensure that this ID corresponds to valid country entries.

name.description: Stores the name of the venue, which is a varchar. This is important for display purposes and should be unique within the context of the same country.

city.description: Stores the city where the venue is located, which is a varchar. This provides geographical context and can be used for filtering or grouping venues by city.

image_path.description: Stores the URL of the venue's image, which is a varchar. This is used for visual representation in applications but does not affect data integrity.

capacity.description: Stores the seating capacity of the venue, which is a bigint. This is a metric that can be used to assess the scale of events held at the venue.

floodlight.description: Stores a boolean value indicating whether the venue has floodlights, represented as a bit. This is important for determining if matches can be played at night.

updated_at.description: Stores the timestamp of the last update to the record, which is a datetime. This is useful for tracking changes and maintaining data accuracy.
